$comment: BMW-specific fault codes, keyed by module id then 4-digit hex code. Every text is written in our own words, never copied from BMW software or documents. 'confidence': high = two or more independent sources agree, medium = one specific source. 'engines' limits a meaning to those engines (the same code can differ between engine computers). 'seenOn' lists real cars where Klemme15 read the code. Generated by tools/research/merge_codes.py from the files in tools/research; edit those, then re-run the script.

93A9.text: Airbag module reports a fault in the driver's seat belt pretensioner igniter circuit.
93A9.hint: Common cause is a loose or damaged connector at the pretensioner (often after seat or trim work).

93C1.text: Airbag module reports a fault with the passenger seat occupancy sensor.
93C1.hint: Check the seat occupancy mat/sensor wiring under the passenger seat.

93C2.text: Airbag module reports a fault with the passenger seat occupancy detection.
93C2.hint: In a documented E90 case the occupancy sensor was unplugged and its cable torn; check its connector, power, ground and LIN line.

93FB.text: Airbag module is not receiving the vehicle-speed message from the DSC.

A0A9.text: The CAS module has detected an internal fault in its own electronics.
A0A9.hint: Often logged together with terminal 15 output faults (A0BE/A0BF/A0C0) and no-start or no-ignition symptoms; common cause is a failing CAS unit, but check battery voltage and CAS power/ground first.

A0AA.text: CAS internal register-monitoring fault; if it keeps recurring the CAS can block engine start and the steering lock.
A0AA.hint: An E90 forum post links it to low voltage during cranking. Clear it, start with a charger/14 V supply connected and see if it returns; then check battery and main cables. Shops reset it with a CAS/ELV reset function.

A0B1.text: CAS sees an implausible gear-selector position (Park/Neutral) input.
A0B1.hint: Often stored without symptoms. If the car won't crank in P/N, check the selector/gearbox P-N signal and wiring to the CAS.

A0B2.text: CAS reports a problem with its own supply voltage (terminal 30 feed).
A0B2.hint: Check battery condition, CAS fuses and the main positive cable connections before suspecting the CAS.

A0B3.text: CAS sees a missing or faulty starter (terminal 50) signal.
A0B3.hint: Check the starter solenoid wire, starter and battery cables; low battery voltage while cranking can also set it.

A0B4.text: CAS reports a fault in the engine start (starter control) function.

A0B5.text: CAS is not getting a valid road-speed signal.
A0B5.hint: The speed comes over the CAN bus from the DSC; look for DSC or CAN faults stored at the same time.

A0BE.text: CAS reports a fault on one of its terminal 15 (ignition) outputs (output 1).
A0BE.hint: Common pattern with A0A9 on a failing CAS, often when warm; check fuses and loads on the terminal 15 circuits first.

A0BF.text: CAS reports a fault on one of its terminal 15 (ignition) outputs (output 2).

A0C0.text: CAS reports a fault on one of its terminal 15 (ignition) outputs (output 3).

A114.text: CAS reports a wiring/line fault to the electric steering lock.

A118.text: CAS finds the road-speed signal implausible (its different inputs disagree).
A118.hint: Usually a side effect of DSC/CAN or low-voltage problems; check for speed-related faults in other modules.

A119.text: CAS reports a problem with the power supply to the electric steering lock.
A119.hint: Check the steering lock fuse/feed and connector; a weak battery can also trigger steering lock faults.

D904.text: CAS reports a K-CAN low-wire physical bus fault.

D907.text: CAS reports its K-CAN bus controller went bus-off.
D907.hint: Usually one of many bus-off codes after a K-CAN wiring short or a failing module; check for the same code in other modules.

E184.text: Head unit reports a K-CAN low-wire fault.

E187.text: Head unit reports a K-CAN bus-off/communication fault.

E18D.text: Head unit failed to wake the bus/network after three attempts.

E18F.text: Head unit's stored list of fitted modules doesn't match the car's target configuration.
E18F.hint: Often appears after retrofits or coding; usually harmless if nothing is missing.

29CC.text: Misfires were detected on more than one cylinder.
29CC.hint: Check the single-cylinder misfire codes stored with it; common causes are worn plugs, coils, vacuum leaks or Valvetronic/injector problems.

29CD.text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 1.
29CD.hint: Swap the cylinder 1 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.

29CE.text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 2.
29CE.hint: Swap the cylinder 2 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.

29CF.text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 3.
29CF.hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

29D0.text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 4.
29D0.hint: Swap the cylinder 4 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.

29D1.text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 5.
29D1.hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

29D2.text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 6.
29D2.hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

29D9.text: Misfires were detected while the fuel tank was nearly empty.
29D9.hint: Refuel and clear the code before chasing ignition or injector faults.

29DC.text: Fuel injection on one or more cylinders was cut because high-pressure fuel rail pressure was too low.
29DC.hint: Classic N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) code, but a weak in-tank low-pressure pump or clogged filter can cause it too; check low-side pressure before buying an HPFP. BMW extended HPFP coverage on many N54 cars (SI B12 55 06).

29E0.text: Fuel mixture control for cylinders 1-3 is out of range, usually because the engine is running lean.
29E0.hint: Common causes are unmetered air (crankcase vent valve, oil filler cap, intake gaskets), a weak fuel supply or a dirty air-mass sensor.

29E1.text: Fuel mixture control for cylinders 4-6 is out of range, usually because the engine is running lean.
29E1.hint: Usually appears together with 29E0; look for vacuum leaks (crankcase vent valve is a common cause) before replacing sensors.

29E2.text: The fuel rail pressure sensor signal is faulty or implausible.
29E2.hint: Can be the rail pressure sensor or wiring, but often logged alongside 29DC when rail pressure genuinely collapses from a failing pump.

29F1.text: Measured high-pressure fuel rail pressure does not make sense compared with what the pump control expects.
29F1.hint: Often stored together with 29F2 or 29DC; diagnose the fuel supply (HPFP, low-pressure pump, rail pressure sensor) as a whole.

29F2.text: High-pressure fuel rail pressure dropped below the target the engine computer asked for.
29F2.hint: Common cause: failing HPFP; also check the low-pressure supply (in-tank pump, filter) since either side can trigger it.

29F3.text: Electrical fault in the low-pressure fuel sensor circuit.
29F3.hint: This is a wiring/sensor fault, not a pressure problem: check the low-pressure sensor and its plug first.

2A2E.text: Fuel mixture adaptation for cylinders 1-3 has reached its limit (reported generically as P0172).
2A2E.hint: Often logged together with 2A2F and the air-mass code 2D06; check for intake leaks and the air-mass sensor.

2A2F.text: Fuel mixture adaptation for cylinders 4-6 has reached its limit (reported generically as P0175).
2A2F.hint: Usually seen with 2A2E; check for intake leaks and the air-mass sensor.

2A37.text: The Valvetronic eccentric shaft position sensor reports values that do not make sense.
2A37.hint: Unplug the eccentric shaft sensor under the valve cover and check for engine oil in the connector; an oil-soaked harness (and sometimes DME connector) is a known cause.

2A38.text: The Valvetronic motor is moving sluggishly or its circuit appears open.
2A38.hint: Check the Valvetronic motor wiring and connector; a failed or seized Valvetronic motor (or a sticking eccentric shaft) is the common cause.

2A3F.text: The Valvetronic servo motor is not getting a proper power supply.
2A3F.hint: Usually causes limp mode. Check battery/charging voltage and the Valvetronic power feed (relay, fuse, wiring) before replacing the motor.

2A47.text: The Valvetronic eccentric shaft position signal is implausible.
2A47.hint: Same known cause as 2A37: oil leaking past the eccentric shaft sensor gasket into its wiring; the valve cover gasket is often leaking too.

2A80.text: Activation fault on the intake VANOS solenoid circuit.
2A80.hint: Check the intake VANOS solenoid connector and wiring, then the solenoid itself.

2A82.text: The intake VANOS (camshaft timing) unit is stiff or mechanically stuck.
2A82.hint: Common cause: a sticking or dirty intake VANOS solenoid; BMW's service bulletin also called for a DME software update on affected cars. Check oil level and condition too.

2A87.text: The exhaust VANOS (camshaft timing) unit is stiff or mechanically stuck.
2A87.hint: Common cause: a sticking or dirty exhaust VANOS solenoid; swapping intake and exhaust solenoids shows whether the fault follows the part.

2A94.text: The engine computer reports a problem with the crankshaft position sensor signal.
2A94.hint: Check the crankshaft sensor connector and wiring at the back of the block before replacing the sensor.

2A98.text: The intake camshaft position relative to the crankshaft is outside the expected range.
2A98.hint: Common causes are a sticking intake VANOS solenoid or low/dirty oil; on high-mileage engines also consider timing chain stretch.

2A99.text: The exhaust camshaft position relative to the crankshaft is outside the expected range.
2A99.hint: Common cause is a sticking exhaust VANOS solenoid; low oil level and timing chain wear are other possibilities.

2A9A.text: The intake camshaft sensor signal cannot be used to synchronise the engine.
2A9A.hint: Can cause long cranking or no-start. Check the intake camshaft sensor and its wiring; a stuck intake VANOS solenoid can also set it.

2A9B.text: The exhaust camshaft sensor signal cannot be used to synchronise the engine.
2A9B.hint: Check the exhaust camshaft sensor and wiring; a stuck exhaust VANOS solenoid is another known cause.

2AA9.text: Activation fault on DISA intake-manifold flap servo motor 2.
2AA9.hint: Check the DISA valve connector and wiring, then the DISA valve itself before considering the intake manifold.

2AAB.text: The DME's self-test of the DISA variable intake system failed.
2AAB.hint: Common cause: a worn or broken DISA valve (flap rattling or stuck); symptoms include rough idle and low power.

2AAC.text: The DME's self-test of DISA variable intake system 2 failed.
2AAC.hint: Common cause: a failed DISA valve; owners often find both valves worn when one code appears.

2AAF.text: The low-pressure (in-tank) fuel supply did not reach the pressure the engine computer requested.
2AAF.hint: Common on tuned cars. If it appears with other fuel codes, check the in-tank fuel pump, fuel filter and the fuel pump control module (EKPS).

2C2B.text: The pre-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 1-3 failed its plausibility/system check.
2C2B.hint: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor and intake air leaks before replacing the sensor.

2C31.text: The pre-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 1-3 has reached its control/trim limit.
2C31.hint: Check for intake or exhaust leaks; an ageing sensor is another common cause.

2C78.text: The post-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 4-6 shows no activity (generic P0160).
2C78.hint: Test the sensor heater and signal wiring before replacing the sensor.

2C7E.text: The post-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 1-3 reports a trim/plausibility problem.
2C7E.hint: The DME could not correct the front sensor using the rear one; check for exhaust leaks and the front sensor as well as the rear sensor.

2C7F.text: The post-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 4-6 reports a trim/plausibility problem.
2C7F.hint: Same diagnosis as 2C7E but for the rear sensor on cylinders 4-6.

2D06.text: The air-mass (intake air metering) system reports implausible values.
2D06.hint: Common cause is unmetered air (vacuum leak, crankcase vent valve, intake boot) rather than the air-mass sensor itself.

2D0F.text: The air-mass sensor signal is faulty or out of range.
2D0F.hint: Check the air-mass sensor connector and for intake leaks; replace the sensor if wiring is good.

2D5A.text: Intake VANOS control fault: the intake camshaft is sticking.
2D5A.hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.

2D5B.text: Intake VANOS control fault: the intake camshaft does not reach its target position.
2D5B.hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.

2D60.text: Exhaust VANOS control fault: the exhaust camshaft is sticking.
2D60.hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.

2D61.text: Exhaust VANOS control fault: the exhaust camshaft does not reach its target position.
2D61.hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.

2D9F.text: Intake camshaft position sensor signal is implausible.
2D9F.hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.

2DA1.text: Exhaust camshaft position sensor signal is implausible.
2DA1.hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.

2DEB.text: Power management in the engine computer logged an on-board electrical system (voltage) fault.
2DEB.hint: Check battery condition and alternator output; one video ties it to alternator over-voltage.

2DEC.text: Engine computer's power management logged a battery problem.
2DEC.hint: Test the battery and make sure a replacement was registered with the right type/capacity.

2DED.text: Power management detected too much current draw while the car was asleep (parasitic drain).
2DED.hint: Look for a module keeping the car awake; in that thread the tailgate wiring harness was damaged.

2E81.text: The electric coolant pump is not running at the speed the engine computer asked for.
2E81.hint: Usually the electric water pump is failing; low coolant or air in the system can also set it. Bleed the system before condemning the pump.

2E82.text: The engine computer has switched the electric coolant pump off.
2E82.hint: Commonly means the electric water pump has failed (e.g. drawing too much current); replacing pump and thermostat together is common practice.

2E83.text: The electric coolant pump is running in reduced-power mode.
2E83.hint: Early sign of a failing electric water pump; also check coolant level and air in the system.

2E84.text: The engine computer cannot communicate with the electric coolant pump.
2E84.hint: Check the pump's connector (corroded pins are common) and the data wire; otherwise the pump is likely faulty.

2E85.text: Communication with the electric coolant pump failed, possibly due to its power supply.
2E85.hint: Check the pump's fuse, power and ground wiring and connector; if they are good, the pump is the usual culprit.

2E8B.text: The engine computer is not getting a valid signal from the intelligent battery sensor (IBS).
2E8B.hint: Check the IBS on the battery negative terminal and its wiring; it often appears after battery work.

2E8C.text: The intelligent battery sensor (IBS) reports an internal function fault.
2E8C.hint: Check the IBS connector and wiring at the battery negative terminal before replacing the sensor.

2E8D.text: Signal transmission from the intelligent battery sensor (IBS) is faulty.
2E8D.hint: Check the IBS data wire and connector at the battery negative terminal.

2E8E.text: The engine computer has lost communication with the intelligent battery sensor (IBS).
2E8E.hint: Check the IBS and its wiring; a weak battery or poor connection at the terminal is a common trigger.

2E98.text: The engine computer cannot communicate properly with the alternator.
2E98.hint: Often logged after battery or alternator work; check the alternator's data connector and wiring, then the alternator voltage regulator.

2E9F.text: Fault with the oil condition (level/quality) sensor.
2E9F.hint: Check the sensor's connector and wiring at the bottom of the oil pan; the sensor itself fails often. Verify oil level with a manual reading since the dash level reading will be unreliable.

2EF4.text: The map-controlled (electrically heated) thermostat has a mechanical fault, e.g. stuck open.
2EF4.hint: Usual fix is a new thermostat; engine running cold or slow warm-up is the typical symptom.

2EF8.text: Activation fault on the map-controlled thermostat's heating element.
2EF8.hint: Check the thermostat connector and wiring; if the code returns after a new thermostat, suspect the harness.

2EFE.text: Activation fault on the electric radiator cooling fan.
2EFE.hint: Check the fan's fuse and large power connector; the fan motor or its built-in controller is the usual failure.

2EFF.text: The electric cooling fan failed its self-diagnosis.
2EFF.hint: A fan stuck at full speed is a typical symptom; the fan/controller assembly usually needs replacing.

2FBC.text: Problem with the signal to the volume control valve on the high-pressure fuel pump.
2FBC.hint: Not a pressure code itself; check the valve's connector and wiring on the HPFP before replacing parts.

2FBE.text: Fuel rail pressure fell away abnormally after the engine was switched off.
2FBE.hint: A single occurrence is often harmless and can be cleared; if it returns with long cranks, suspect the HPFP or a leaking injector.

2FBF.text: Fuel rail pressure was too low at the moment injection was enabled during start-up.
2FBF.hint: Usually shows as long cranking. BMW's first fix was a DME software update; persistent cases point to the HPFP or low-pressure supply.

300C.text: Intake camshaft position sensor signal is too high (electrical).
300C.hint: Check the sensor connector and wiring; the BMW bulletin links it to VANOS adjuster failure on early N55.

300D.text: Intake camshaft position sensor signal is too low (electrical).
300D.hint: Check the sensor connector and wiring; the BMW bulletin links it to VANOS adjuster failure on early N55.

300E.text: Exhaust camshaft position sensor signal is too high (electrical).
300E.hint: Check the sensor connector and wiring; the BMW bulletin links it to VANOS adjuster failure on early N55.

300F.text: Exhaust camshaft position sensor signal is too low (electrical).
300F.hint: Check the sensor connector and wiring; the BMW bulletin links it to VANOS adjuster failure on early N55.

30BE.text: Injector calibration values stored in the engine computer are implausible.
30BE.hint: Typical after injector replacement: the new injectors' calibration (IMA) codes must be entered into the DME.

30CF.text: Problem with the wastegate control input signal.
30CF.hint: Most often an unplugged wastegate/boost solenoid connector or loose wiring, sometimes caused by a piggyback tuning module.

30FE.text: Boost (charge-air) pressure is higher than the engine computer expects (overboost).
30FE.hint: Common causes: tuning, or boost solenoids/vacuum control letting the wastegates close too much.

30FF.text: Boost (charge-air) pressure is lower than the engine computer expects (underboost).
30FF.hint: Common causes: boost leaks in charge pipe/intercooler/diverter valves, cracked wastegate vacuum lines, faulty boost solenoids, worn or rattling wastegates, or a failing turbo.

3100.text: Boost pressure control has been switched off, so the engine runs without boost.
3100.hint: Usually a follow-on fault: read the other stored codes (VANOS, overheating, boost faults) and fix those first; alone it may just need clearing.

5D90.text: DSC reports a fault with the front-left wheel speed sensor signal.
5D90.hint: Check the sensor connector and wiring at the front-left hub, then the sensor itself.

5D96.text: DSC reports an implausible direction-of-rotation signal from the front-left wheel speed sensor.
5D96.hint: Common cause is a failing or wrong-type wheel speed sensor at the front left.

5DA0.text: DSC reports a fault with the front-right wheel speed sensor.
5DA0.hint: Inspect the front-right sensor, its wiring and connector.

5DA1.text: DSC reports a fault with the front-right wheel speed sensor signal.
5DA1.hint: Inspect the front-right sensor, its wiring and connector.

5DA6.text: DSC reports a fault with the front-right wheel speed sensor.
5DA6.hint: Common cause is a failing front-right wheel speed sensor.

5DB0.text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor.
5DB0.hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

5DB1.text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor signal.
5DB1.hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

5DB2.text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor signal.
5DB2.hint: On an E91 335i the cause was a worn rear wheel bearing (the sensor reads the bearing's encoder ring).

5DB3.text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor.
5DB3.hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

5DB6.text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor.
5DB6.hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

5DC0.text: DSC reports an electrical fault in the power supply of the rear-right wheel speed sensor.
5DC0.hint: Check the rear-right sensor wiring for shorts or chafing and measure supply voltage at the connector before replacing the sensor.

5DC1.text: DSC finds the rear-right wheel speed sensor signal implausible.
5DC1.hint: Inspect the rear-right sensor, its encoder ring and wiring.

5DC3.text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-right wheel speed sensor.
5DC3.hint: Inspect the rear-right sensor, wiring and connector.

5DC6.text: DSC reports an implausible direction-of-rotation signal from the rear-right wheel speed sensor.
5DC6.hint: Common cause is a failing or incorrect rear-right wheel speed sensor.

5DF0.text: The ABS/DSC hydraulic unit reports a fault with its electric pump motor.
5DF0.hint: Check the DSC unit's ground and power first; common cause is worn pump motor brushes or a failing motor, often fixed by rebuilding or replacing the hydraulic unit.

5DF1.text: The ABS/DSC hydraulic unit reports a problem at the pump motor's electrical connection.
5DF1.hint: Common cause is a poor contact or corroded/burnt connector between pump motor and DSC control board; check the unit's ground strap before buying parts.

5E18.text: DSC is not getting the data it expects from the engine computer over the CAN bus.
5E18.hint: Often logged after a low or disconnected battery or engine computer work; clear it and see if it returns.

5E19.text: DSC has detected a problem in its communication or torque-control interface with the engine computer.
5E19.hint: Often a follow-on of an engine fault that puts the car in limp mode; read and fix the DME codes first.

5E20.text: The pressure sensor built into the ABS/DSC hydraulic unit has failed or gives an implausible reading.
5E20.hint: The sensor is internal to the hydraulic unit, so the usual fix is repairing or replacing the DSC unit; rule out low battery voltage first.

5E50.text: The steering angle sensor needs to be calibrated (zero-point / serial number adjustment) to the DSC.
5E50.hint: Run the steering angle sensor adjustment with wheels straight and steering wheel level; needed after SZL, DSC or alignment work.

5EBA.text: DSC finds the steering angle sensor signal implausible compared with other vehicle data.
5EBA.hint: In a documented E90 case the cause was a damaged code disc inside the steering column switch cluster (SZL), not the DSC.

5F12.text: Brake pad wear warning from the front-axle pad wear sensor.
5F12.hint: Check front pad thickness; the wear sensor must be replaced with the pads and the service interval reset.

5F15.text: DSC finds the rear-axle brake pad wear sensor signal implausible.
5F15.hint: Check rear pad thickness and the rear wear sensor wiring; replace the sensor with new pads.

94B5.text: DSC logged an internal fault of the steering column switch cluster (SZL).
94B5.hint: Common cause in the documented case was a damaged steering angle code disc in the SZL.

94BB.text: DSC logged an internal fault reported by the steering angle sensor.
94BB.hint: The steering angle sensor sits in the steering column switch cluster (SZL); inspect the SZL before replacing the DSC.

4F81.text: The gearbox computer detected an incorrect gear ratio involving internal clutch A (slip).
4F81.hint: Check fluid level and condition; persistent clutch slip codes may point to worn clutch packs.

4F84.text: The gearbox computer detected an incorrect gear ratio involving internal clutch D (slip).
4F84.hint: Check fluid level and condition; persistent clutch slip codes may point to worn clutch packs.

4F85.text: The gearbox computer detected an incorrect gear ratio involving internal clutch E (slip).
4F85.hint: Can be clutch wear or low hydraulic pressure; check fluid level and condition before condemning the gearbox.

4F8A.text: The gearbox computer saw the wrong gear ratio during the 4th-to-5th upshift.
4F8A.hint: Check transmission fluid level and condition; may indicate clutch wear.

4F8C.text: The gearbox computer saw the wrong gear ratio during the 6th-to-5th downshift.
4F8C.hint: Identifies a failed shift event, not necessarily a dead gearbox; check fluid and adaptations.

4F8D.text: The gearbox computer saw the wrong gear ratio during the 5th-to-4th downshift.
4F8D.hint: Common causes are old or low transmission fluid, mechatronic sleeve leaks or worn clutches; check fluid level and condition first.

5079.text: Intermittent gearbox faults and emergency mode caused by an incorrectly fitted mechatronic connector sleeve.
5079.hint: BMW service bulletin SI B 24 08 06 covers this on ZF 6HP gearboxes; inspect or replace the sleeve and refill fluid.

507A.text: Intermittent gearbox faults and emergency mode caused by an incorrectly fitted mechatronic connector sleeve.
507A.hint: See BMW SI B 24 08 06; inspect or replace the sleeve and refill fluid.

931D.text: Footwell module reports the steering column left turn-signal switch input faulty.

931E.text: Footwell module reports the steering column right turn-signal switch input faulty.

931F.text: Footwell module reports the steering column high-beam/flasher switch input faulty.

9CAB.text: Footwell module reports the terminal 15 (ignition on) signal is missing.

9CAF.text: Footwell module reports a fault on light switch position 1.

9CB0.text: Footwell module reports a fault on light switch position 2.

9CB5.text: Footwell module logged a flat/exhausted battery condition.
9CB5.hint: Charge or test the battery; usually set after the car sat or was jump-started.

9CB6.text: Footwell module found an open circuit in a headlight height (vertical aim) adjuster motor.
9CB6.hint: Check the headlight leveling motor and its connector.

9CB8.text: Footwell module switched off the parking/side lights to protect a discharging battery.

9CBA.text: Footwell module lost communication with a LIN-bus control unit (such as the light switch).

9CC3.text: Footwell module lost communication with the driver-side mirror.

9CC4.text: Footwell module lost communication with the passenger-side mirror.

9CC5.text: Footwell module reports the driver-side mirror heater faulty.

9CCD.text: Footwell module reports the driver-side mirror adjustment motor faulty.

9CCE.text: Footwell module reports the passenger-side mirror adjustment motor faulty.

A8AC.text: Footwell module reports the front left side-marker/parking light faulty (open circuit).

A8AE.text: Footwell module reports the left front fog light circuit faulty (left daytime running light on M3).
A8AE.hint: Check the bulb and connector first.

A8AF.text: Footwell module reports the right front fog light circuit faulty (right daytime running light on M3).
A8AF.hint: Check the bulb and connector first.

A8B2.text: Footwell module reports the left rear turn signal faulty.

A8B6.text: Footwell module reports the left brake light faulty.

A8B7.text: Footwell module reports the right brake light faulty.

A8C3.text: Footwell module reports the third brake light / left adaptive brake light faulty.

A8C4.text: Footwell module reports the third brake light / right adaptive brake light faulty.

A8C5.text: Footwell module reports the left daytime running light faulty.
A8C5.hint: On cars with angel-eye DRLs check the ring bulb/LED and its connector.

A8C6.text: Footwell module reports the right daytime running light faulty.

E584.text: Footwell module reports a K-CAN low-wire fault.

E594.text: Footwell module is not receiving the steering-angle message.

E597.text: Footwell module is not receiving messages from the DSC.

E599.text: Footwell module is not receiving the road-speed message from the DSC.

A088.text: Roof function centre reports a fault with the sunroof switch.

A090.text: Roof function centre reports a sunroof mechanism fault.

A092.text: Sunroof needs or failed its normalization (initialization).
A092.hint: Common after battery disconnects; re-initialize the sunroof by holding the switch.

A669.text: Roof function centre reports a fault in the front interior light circuit.
A669.hint: Check the front interior/reading lamps and their wiring in the roof console.

A670.text: Roof function centre reports a fault with the windscreen condensation (fogging) sensor.
A670.hint: Often the sensor behind the mirror has come loose or its connector is bad; replacing the FZD or rain sensor alone may not fix it.

9C6C.text: Climate control reports a fault on the 12 V supply to the centre console switch centre.

E704.text: Climate control reports a K-CAN wiring fault.

E707.text: Climate control's CAN controller went bus-off.

E714.text: Climate control got a faulty or missing terminal-status message from the CAS.

A6D0.text: Junction box reports a fault in the A/C compressor control valve circuit.

A731.text: Junction box reports a problem with the terminal 30g_f supply circuit.
A731.hint: Terminal 30g_f feeds modules like the head unit; check the relay/fuses and battery state.

A738.text: Junction box reports that its power supply was interrupted.

C907.text: Junction box reports its K-CAN controller went bus-off.

C908.text: Junction box reports PT-CAN bus-off / K-CAN running on a single wire.

C90B.text: Junction box reports a PT-CAN communication fault.

C91E.text: Junction box is not receiving the terminal-status message from the CAS.

9315.text: The mileage stored in the instrument cluster and its backup copy in another module don't agree.

9319.text: The cluster reports a fault with the left fuel level sender.

931A.text: The cluster reports a fault with the right fuel level sender.

931B.text: The cluster reports a fault with the outside temperature sensor.

931D.text: The instrument cluster saw supply voltage that was too high or too low.
931D.hint: Common cause: weak battery or charging problem.

A3AC.text: The cluster got a faulty or missing distance-travelled message from the DSC.

A3AD.text: The cluster got a faulty engine-data message from the engine computer.

A3AE.text: The cluster got a faulty engine-speed (RPM) message from the engine computer.

A3AF.text: The cluster got a faulty speed set-point (cruise control) message from the engine side.

A3B2.text: The cluster got a faulty terminal-status (ignition state) message from the CAS on the CAN bus.
A3B2.hint: Usually a side effect of low battery voltage, a CAS problem or a bus fault; check battery and main power connections and look for CAS faults.

A3B4.text: The cluster got a faulty lighting-status message from the footwell module (FRM).
A3B4.hint: Commonly appears with A3C1 when the FRM has failed or lost its coding/data (lights, indicators and windows dead).

A3B9.text: The cluster got a faulty or missing stability-control (DSC) status message on the CAN bus.
A3B9.hint: Look at the DSC fault memory and its supply/CAN wiring; often appears with other DSC message faults.

A3BB.text: The cluster got a faulty door-status message from the CAS.

A3BD.text: The cluster got a faulty message from the junction box (JBE).

A3C0.text: The cluster got a faulty message from the trailer module.

A3C1.text: The cluster is not receiving a valid message from the footwell module (FRM).
A3C1.hint: Check FRM fuses and power; a failed or corrupted FRM is a common cause.

A54B.text: The cluster got a faulty electric power steering message.

A550.text: The cluster got a faulty or missing vehicle-speed message from the DSC.

A559.text: The instrument cluster logged that its power supply was switched off or interrupted.
A559.hint: Check battery voltage and the cluster supply; often logged after battery disconnects or low voltage.

A560.text: The cluster got a faulty or missing gear-shift indicator message from the engine computer.

A562.text: The cluster got a faulty auto start-stop (MSA) status message from the engine computer.

E104.text: The cluster reports a K-CAN low-wire fault.
E104.hint: Usually logged by many modules at once; look for a K-CAN short or a faulty module dragging the bus down.

E107.text: The cluster's CAN controller went bus-off.

E204.text: Park distance control reports a K-CAN low-wire or interruption fault.

E207.text: Park distance control reports its CAN controller went bus-off.
